newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kazakhstan alarmed over "aggresive secessionism".
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan alarmed over "aggresive secessionism".

text.p: The foreign minister of Kazakhstan expressed alarm Friday at what he called "aggressive secessionism" and said it was time to end the absolute right of nations to self-determination.
"When we talk about international issues we cannot ignore such an alarming trend as growing secessionism," Kasymzhomart Tokayev said in a speech to the General Assembly.
This had become one of the major causes of crises, particularly in parts of the former Soviet Union, he said.

"We think that the U.N. has to pay close attention to the destructive consequences of an aggressive secessionism...Time has come to put an end to the absolutization of the right of nations to self-determination," he said, opposing a principle that was an article of faith with many U.N. members during the era of decolonization.
"Basically, the world has already realised the right to self-determination. Further continuation of this process will create new trouble spots and will lead to more bloodshed," Tokaev said.
He did not cite any examples.
In countries of the former Soviet Union alone, secessionist movements have arisen in the Chechnya region of Russia, Azerbaijan's Armenian-populated Nagorno Karabakh and the Abkhaz region of Georgia.
Tokaev said the world order should rest on the principles of sovereignty and the territorial integrity of states.
"If we really care about the stability of the current world order, we must all firmly reject any manifestations of secessionism."

The highest values should become peace, well-being and the happiness of the people, he said, adding: ""We can achieve these goals not by instigating to self-determination but through the creation of appropriate conditions for sustainable economic development of all nations."
